title: Stoichiometry silently accepts unbalanced equations and returns wrong yields
repro_steps: On zuko_qa_t1, /lenses/chem > Structure > Stoichiometry: enter 'H2 + O2 -> H2O' with H2 4 g, O2 40 g. Repeat with 'Fe + O2 -> Fe2O3' (Fe 4 g) and 'C3H8 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O' (C3H8 4 g).
expected: Reject or auto-balance an unbalanced equation. Correct answers: 2H2+O2->2H2O gives H2 limiting, 35.74 g H2O; 4Fe+3O2->2Fe2O3 gives 5.72 g Fe2O3; C3H8+5O2->3CO2+4H2O gives 11.98 g CO2 and 6.54 g H2O.
actual: Treats every coefficient as 1 with no warning: H2O 22.52 g with O2 as limiting reagent (wrong reagent, 37% low); Fe2O3 11.44 g (2x high); CO2 3.99 g and H2O 1.63 g (3x and 4x low). With the balanced '2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O' the output is correct (35.744 g, O2 leftover 0.258 mol / 8.256 g). Students will get confidently wrong answers.
fix_note: Stoichiometry now counts atoms on both sides of the equation with the same parser as the molecular-weight pass and refuses an unbalanced equation, naming the first element that does not balance. Before, H2 + O2 -> H2O returned yields as if correct.

title: Fact check returns Unverifiable with 0 sources for a textbook-true claim
repro_steps: On /lenses/grounding as zuko_qa_t1, confirm /api/auth/me, then run Fact check on the benign, checkable claim "Water boils at 100 °C at sea level". Record the verdict, confidence, and source count. Inspect the Audit trail for this check and any earlier checks.
expected: A textbook-true claim at standard conditions should be judged true or supported, with sources cited, and a useful answer should mention that boiling point depends on pressure (about 1 atm at sea level). It should not return Unverifiable with no sources.
actual: The verdict came back "Unverifiable", with no confidence and 0 sources (rw-fact-check.png, clock 10:15 PM ET). The claim is true at about 1 atm, and a good answer would mention the pressure dependency. The Audit trail recorded this check at 10:11:27 PM ET as unverifiable with 0 sources, and also shows an earlier check, "The Earth orbits the Sun.", at 8:29:34 PM ET, likewise unverifiable with 0 sources (rw-audit-trail.png).
note: Related still: evidence/grounding/rw-audit-trail.png. Source tier on the same claim, with the NIST Chemistry WebBook (https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C7732185&Mask=4, typed as government), was rated "CREDIBLE (74)" / 74/100 with only the generic reasoning "Consider diversifying source types for better triangulation" (rw-source-tier.png and the same rw-fact-check.png workbench). The rating itself is acceptable; the reasoning is generic (low note, folded into this ticket rather than filed separately). Account zuko_qa_t1. Rework walk 2026-11-12 10:21 PM ET.
fix_note: factCheck, sourceCredibility and claimDecomposition read only artifact.data while the ClaimVerificationPanel sends its input as run params, so every check ran on empty strings. The handlers now read both shapes; panel input and artifact input return identical verdicts.

title: Non-admin sees enabled instance-wide-looking controls and an admin-only route, with no confirm or UI role gating (UX/trust)
repro_steps: On /lenses/federation as zuko_qa_t1 (role member), open Sync, Actor keys, Metrics, and the Network trust graph. Inspect Run sync now, Register key, the Metrics count fields, and the on-screen POST /api/federation/register copy. Do not click the enabled controls.
expected: Instance-wide or admin-only actions are hidden or disabled for a member, with role gating in the UI. Copy that describes key rotation or instance peer registration should match what the action actually does. Privileged-looking actions should ask for confirm.
actual: A member sees enabled Run sync now (copy: triggers a federation pass that pulls shadow DTUs from peers, pushes pending posts, and refreshes peer last-seen timestamps) and enabled + Register key (copy: "Register each peer's signing key. Re-registering a different key rotates it and preserves the prior fingerprint."). Metrics shows editable inbound/outbound count fields and a Record control in a form that reads as instance activity volume. The Network trust graph tells the user to use POST /api/federation/register to peer with another instance. None of these controls showed a confirm, and nothing indicated they were admin-only or per-user. The controls were not clicked. Coordinator code check (Zuko, live tree 7d522b454): the server side is guarded. POST /api/federation/register and /remove return 403 admin_only unless the role is admin or sovereign. registerActorKey, sync policy, and recordMetric are keyed to the calling user's own map and do not change anything instance-wide. POST /api/federation/sync has no registered federation.sync macro and returns federation_sync_unavailable. This is therefore a medium UX/trust issue, not a confirmed authorization hole: the UI exposes enabled controls that look instance-wide, shows an admin-only route, has no confirm and no role gating, and the 'rotates keys' copy is misleading because Register key only updates that user's own key record.
suspected_area: Federation UI role gating and copy (UX/trust)
note: Controls were not clicked. Client authorization was not re-tested; server behavior is from the coordinator code check (Zuko, live tree 7d522b454). Related missing-confirm ticket: FIX-federation-002. Account zuko_qa_t1.
fix_note: Every control the ticket names acts on per-user state, and the peering route is admin-gated server-side (403 admin_only) — the defect was the trust surface: 'Run sync now' POSTed /api/federation/sync, a route that does not exist, under instance-wide copy; the key book and the metrics log read as instance administration; the trust graph pointed members at the admin-only register route as their peering path. The dead sync trigger is removed (sync runs on the server's cycle; the panel now shows the recorded event log), and the key book, metrics and peering copy state their real scope.

title: Feed Export includes another user's private record
repro_steps: On /lenses/feed as zuko_qa_t1, use Export to download JSON and CSV. Open the JSON bundle and inspect each record's id, title, visibility, and owner id only; do not copy record bodies.
expected: A signed-in user's Feed export should include only that user's own records and records that are meant to be public or otherwise shared with them. It must not include another user's private record.
actual: The JSON export contained 17 records: 12 public product-recall DTUs, 3 public posts owned by other users, 1 content-controls record for t1, and one private record owned by another user — id lart_12590a4ce7a550ead863, title 'PR4 Feed Review 2026-10-31', visibility private, owner id prefix 0a6c582d. The CSV also includes that record's id and title (flat id/title/type/createdAt/updatedAt; no body column). The record body is not copied here. t1 ownership was checked against t1's own private Daily export record, which does not match this owner prefix.
note: Related: FIX-meditation-001 and FIX-export-011 (other users' export leakage). Zuko was notified at 12:21 AM ET for a code check and confirmed the finding independently at 12:21 AM ET. The export JSON is kept only in evidence/feed/. Account zuko_qa_t1.
fix_note: The walker's path is GET /api/lens/feed/export/download (routes/universal-export.js), which funnels into collectLensExport in server/lib/lens-export.js. Its artifact leg takes whatever the lens.list macro returns. lens.list applies its ownership/visibility filter only to non-social domains — 'feed' sits in its SOCIAL_DOMAINS set, so for the feed domain the macro returns every artifact in the domain store with no owner or visibility check at all. The export's own filters caught only dispatcher scaffolding and activity-minted mirrors, so a genuine private artifact owned by another user (the walk's lart_ record, visibility private) rode the bundle in both JSON and CSV. The other three legs were checked and are sound: the feed export provider reads only the caller's buckets, exportCallerLensState reads only the caller's bucket, and the DTU leg already drops other users' DTUs by owner. Fix, at the shared export layer so every lens's export inherits it: the artifact leg now applies the takeout scope itself — an artifact owned by another user rides only when its visibility is public or published; the caller's own records ride at any visibility; ownerless public-catalog rows keep riding, as the 2026-11-09 hotfix intends. lens.list itself is unchanged: the social open-square rule is a deliberate, repeated read-layer decision (lens.get and _lensArtifactVisible carry the same rule) that feed rendering relies on; the takeout contract is the export's own. Guard: server/tests/lens-export-artifact-scope.test.js, 3/3 on the fixed tree, 3/3 failing at pristine; 69 neighbouring export tests green (affect/clf/crisis/entity providers, private-filter, domain-parity). Related tickets FIX-meditation-001 and FIX-export-011 (named in this ticket's note) ride other export paths and were not in this assignment.
